strings.BOL_paternalism_party_long: Alianza Institucionalista Democrática (Partido de la Unión Republicana Socialista)
strings.BOL_Alfredo_Mollinedo_hog_desc:
Vice President
Oligarchy
--------------
There is little to know about the grey suit that holds the Vice Presidency of Bolivia, other than that it was a good pick for the job. Originally the Vice President of the board of directors of la Paz in 1933, Alfredo Mollinedo would become the first Minister of Health of Bolivia in 1938 under Butch. However, his later contributions to Bolivian football are for what he is known for, as his AFLP led the charge of professionalization. This era saw him locked in a struggle with Alfredo Galindo, the manager of the rival FBF, but it was a conflict that Mollinedo would come victorious from.

Being a PURS party man, he quickly found himself in the list of possible Vice Presidents of Terrazas because of the electoral pact between PURS and the PL, and ultimately, he was chosen because of his name recognition among Bolivians, which AID policy makers expected could give the new oligarchic government some of the much-needed goodwill from the population.
strings.BOL_Mamerto_Urriolagoitia_for_desc:
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Oligarchy
--------------
Angry, putrid, old, those are words that could describe Mamerto Urriolagoitía and his present situation. Born into money, he studied law and with the typical Francophilia of the Latin American aristocracy, he moved to the Gallic country to study international law. He had a bright future ahead of him, and being chosen as Hertzog's Vice President brought him close to the halls of power. He committed the sin however of trying to usurp his president, and the even more grave sin of failing at this task, which turned him into a black sheep inside the PURS.

He still commanded the loyalty of some hardliners inside the party, but with his chances at the presidency dead, the only post his supporters could assure him was being the Minister of Foreign Affairs, an area in which he had some experience as he had been a delegate to London in the past. But Urriolagoitía has seen his appointment as an exile and dislikes diplomacy, feeling envious that he isn't in charge of the repression, because he believes he could do a better job at it.
strings.BOL_Antenor_Patino_eco_desc:
Minister of Economic Affairs and Public Finance
Oligarchy
--------------
Grab a Marxist, a liberal and a fascist and they will tell you the same: the fact that Antenor Patiño is in the government, worst of all as the finance minister, is the greatest insult to the exploited Bolivian working class.

One of the richest men in the Americas, Patiño has the honor of being the heir of his father Simón, “the king of Tin”. Such a title isn't a joke by any means, his family owns the majority of the tin mines in Bolivia and are key players of this resource in the global market, not to speak of how Patiño is related to literal nobility through his marriage to María Cristina de Borbón, the Duchess of Durcal.

Brought into the government under the excuse of a technocratic appointment, Patiño has not wasted any time in showing what “technocracy” means in Bolivia. The government being oligarchic not being enough, the elites have decided that the oligarchs should have direct ownership of the government. After all, a government should be made up of the people they represent.
strings.BOL_Alberto_Crespo_Carpio_sec_desc:
Minister of Defence
Despotism
--------------
The Commander of the Military College from 1950 to 1951, general Alberto Crespo Carpio has certainly already fulfilled his duty to the country. His appointment as the Minister of National Defense comes because of his already proven loyalty to his country and the Oligarchs, as if there is a problem in the Bolivian Armed Forces after years of revolutions and counterrevolutions is which generals to trust.

Under his recommendations Ovando Candía was appointed Chief of the Army, for his perceived moderation, but Crespo Carpio has come to regret his choice when in private conversation the general has spoke to him of the necessity of reform in Bolivia and how the Oligarchs aren't going to implement them. He has remained silent on the issue however, as he feels he is too old to involve himself in a struggle against the Chief of the Army, and at this point he just wants his term to end so that he can enjoy his retirement.
strings.BOL_Mining_War_desc:
The oligarchy has been hanged by the rope they sold, a tattered treaty pinned to its chest, as a military man stands by its gallows facing a crowd still baying for blood.

An outbreak of miners swapping pickaxes for guns appears to be the starting pistol for the rise of a revolution, with all sides taking bets for which way the cards will fall. Out of necessity or a bending of a knee to the milicos, Brazil props up the Ovando dictatorship with bombs and bullets, levelling dissent to a desert called peace.

On the opposition, the Argentines have thrown their weight behind the MNR — led by the former failed dictator Gualberto Villarroel — trumpeting a mishmash of militarism, nationalism, and populism that has attracted an unwanted left-wing element. Competing for these affects is Chile, supporting the FSB — Falangist militias and rightist veterans of lost wars — lighting the final fuse for an unfettered bloodbath.
strings.BOL_patchwork_country_desc:
In Bolivia there are Indians, there are Mestizos, there are Criollos, but there aren't Bolivians. The failure to properly centralize the nation has also led to failure in uniting the various ethnicities under one flag. The Separatists taking over in Santa Cruz has only added fuel to the fire, as propaganda and Bolivian retaliation has ignited all the Orient with talks of secession. To make things worse unrest has also spread to the natives, as the growing Indianist movement keeps winning acolytes who dream about Pachakuti.

To reverse this, to make people want to feel Bolivian and be proud, La Paz waves the flag of revanchism by stating that Santa Cruz will be retaken, that the entire Chaco will be retaken. Five Chaco Wars have come and gone without either of them being returned, but what's another string to the bow right?
strings.BOL_killing_hope_desc:
In the 30s, the peasants thought that Military Socialism would save them, but then Santa Cruz fell and a bullet crossed Busch's brain. The Oligarchs returned. In the 40s Villarroel announced to the people that he would save them, but he was overthrown before he could announce what his project was. And the Oligarchs returned. So did Villarroel, this time as a Military Socialist, as the proud heir of Toro and Busch, but he was removed after military failures. La Paz was soon under the Oligarchs again.

Where does this leave the people? Worse than before: hopeless, because they know that the Oligarchs are untouchable, that the Tin Barons are Gods, that the Patiños, Hochschilds and Aramayos will never face justice.

They know that if one wants a picture of the future, they have to imagine a boot stamping on a human face—forever.
strings.BOL_jose_lanzas_lament_desc:
In the fires of the First Chaco War, General José Lanza, witnessing how the Bolivian army was more concerned with plotting and personal interests than defeating the enemy said the following immortal words:

“I am ashamed of being a Bolivian general!”

If only he was alive to see how things are now! How thankful he must be that he was spared the view of an army completely broken after years of revolutions and counter-revolutions. In fact, such disastrous is the state of the armed forces in Bolivia, that only a Foreign Military Mission can fix it. But then the question is raised.

Who will be the foreign power hired to do it?
strings.BOL_tripartite_pact_desc:
The Tripartite Pact is the name given to a series of treaties signed during Carlos Crespo's interim presidency that secured the neutrality of Bolivia in the South American Cold War. The catch? The country being more or less equally divided for exploitation by Argentina, Brazil, and Chile.

With the backing of the ABC countries being the only thing that secures the rule of the Oligarchs, they are quite happy with this state of affairs, a beautiful symphony in which rivers of money flows to La Paz while all the costs are paid by the backs of the working class. Beautiful, isn't it?
strings.BOL_The_Shadow_War_desc:
Conspiracy theories around the Freemasons and their lodges have been a recurring trend in the Western world ever since they first came to prominence. Oftentimes, such conspiracies are wrapped in a dressing of anti-semitism - most prominently, of course, in the German Reich, where Hitler's decrying of the Masons as a Jewish puppet organization directly led to the state-organized mass murder of its members. Rumors of “Masonic plots” have become a boogeyman of leaders from all sides of the political spectrum who need a convenient scapegoat for their nation's woes, regardless of veracity or consequences.

It is some sort of cruel irony that the only part of the world where this conspiratorial thinking holds any truth is one where its two lodges have long ago splintered away from Masonry altogether.

The “Caballeros del Oriente” and the “Toborochi”, once one and the same until the Toborochi split from the Caballeros, are engaged in a brutal shadow war which engulfs Cruzeño politics. The leadership are all members. The wealthy are all members. The generals are all members. The powerful are all members. If you want to go anywhere in Santa Cruz's society, you will swear yourself to a lodge, or you will find yourself rooted right to where you started.
strings.BOL_A_New_Bolivian_Nationalism_STC_desc: La Paz has finally done it: the separatists in the Orient have been crushed, and vile Paraguay's ambitions turned to ash. Reintegrating the Cruceño separatists will be no easy task, but this is a triumph that all Bolivians, regardless of their color or background, can take pride in. After thirty years of losses, Bolivia's future is becoming brighter.
strings.BOL_A_New_Bolivian_Nationalism_Chaco_des:
Latin America and the world can only look on in awe as the Bolivian people have accomplished the impossible: not only have they reclaimed their wayward East, but they have driven the Paraguayan army so far back that they have reclaimed the Chaco. Racial and class divides are being eroded as a new Bolivian nationalism emerges, and for the first time in living memory, the people are proud to be Bolivian.

Loor eterno a los bravos guerreros,
cuyo heroico valor y firmeza,
conquistaron las glorias que empieza
hoy Bolivia feliz a gozar
strings.BOL_Decalogue_Of_The_Falangist_desc:
1) Love your country above all selfishness.
2) Dedicate yourself absolutely and eternally to the cause of the movement, which is the cause of Bolivia.
3) Respect religious convictions.
4) Be aware of discipline, which is the subordination of the person to the service of the community.
5) Fulfill your duty for the love of duty and not for the reward.
6) Improve yourself every day, because the workers of great causes are first builders of themselves.
7) Disdain life if you sacrifice it for your ideal.
8) Do not retreat or be a coward.
9) Be worthy, loyal and willing to sacrifice.
10) Disdain the comfortable life. A Falangist is above all a fighter. Fight and you will win!

-FSB Principles Program
strings.BOL_The_Infernos_Beating_Heart_desc:
Hell on earth. Minimal food, bare lodgings, dedicated torture chambers, and walls pockmarked with bullet holes. These are the concentration camps of Bolivia's Revolutionary Nationalist Movement.

The MNR regime's secret police, the Control Político, keeps the new blood flowing in. Any threat, any opposition to the MNR is thrown in the back of a truck and driven, choking on exhaust, to their new home. To a steady beat, a new batch of graves appear along the perimeter, and a new set of falangists, communists, journalists, intellectuals, and miscreants take vacant bunks.

And as the revolution grows, so too does the Control Político, its frightened prey, and Bolivia's network of camps.
strings.BOL_The_Caudillo_Of_The_Revolution_desc:
Villarroel is more than just a military strongman; he is the heart and soul of the Bolivian nationalist movement. Both a fervent patriot and an effective revolutionary, he had proven to be not merely another out-of-touch politician through a firm hand and fair administration, bringing thousands out of poverty and punishing the wicked. Beloved by both the impoverished and the liberated natives, his support base is that of a broad and newly emancipated peasantry.

This illustrious image of a hero formed a robust cult of personality surrounding the colonel, yet as internal party division grows in the background, a looming air of breakdown continues tarnishing Villarroel's perceived competence despite his endless repertoire of rhetorics and populist tricks.
strings.BOL_A_Silent_Democracy_desc:
The fading spirit of revolution gave birth to something with far greater potential and longevity — the liberal-democratic order. Enforcing the tradition of the rule of law posited by Western philosophers, Paz Estenssoro, for the first time in many decades, manages to bring stability to Bolivia.

Working behind the scene to ensure the MNR's survival while guiding Bolivia to self-determination. Estenssoro has managed to muzzle most oppositional elements to consolidate the party's hegemony before the people can partake in the electoral process. In these first steps taken by the Bolivian democracy, it is up to the MNR to maintain the fledgling state's fragile national security.
strings.BOL_A_New_Synthesis_desc:
Following the footsteps of David Toro and German Bush, the MNR's founding was a lofty pursuit to extol law and order through the ideological framework of Military Socialism. As years went by, however, the many internal fracturings that inevitably occurred within the party's big tent context seemed to have transformed it into a dysfunctional mess no better than any other failed movements.

Forced to embrace change under dire circumstances, a new synthesis, born from a fusion of Argentine Justicialism with traditional Bolivian patriotism, came about to bring unity back to the factionalized MNR. The people now see Villarroel as the man who aligned the stars into a harmonious existence, yet a question remains in the colonel's heart.

Will the future generations forgive a traitor?
strings.BOL_The_Popular_Assembly_desc:
The Popular Assembly is the organization of the Bolivian unionist, labor, and popular movements that seeks to establish its own organ of power to replace the bourgeois parliament. In many respects, it is akin to a workers' council, and right-wing foreign press has taken to labeling it as a “Soviet.”

The Popular Assembly, while smeared as communist, hasn't actually established any form of a socialist regime. Despite what critics may say, capitalism, albeit in a more limited form, still exists within Bolivia.
strings.BOL_A_Revolutionary_Dictatorship_desc:
The Popular Assembly was a joke, and not a particularly funny one. Dirtbags who don't even shower shouldn't be rulers-can't be rulers. It'd be a disaster to let them have free reign over the country.

Luckily for Bolivia, the good general has removed them from power and put them back where they belong. As he did so, he gave them a generous bargain: They can support his new regime, or else. After all, everybody knows that only the good men of the armed forces are qualified to actually carry out the progressive national revolution Bolivia has needed for so long.
strings.BOL_The_Soviet_Republic_desc:
Lechín's false reformist project crashed and burned into ash, and from its corpse the fires of revolution burn once more. The new republic that has risen is governed by the immortal science of Bolshevik-Leninism and the POR, with Guillermo Lora at its helm.

Now the people of Bolivia will experience true liberation under proper socialism. No longer shall they be at the mercy of leeches, nor the petit bourgeoisie of the treacherous unions. The Bolivian Socialist Soviet Republic is prepared to defend its people against all threats to the revolution. Let it be known that Bolivia is red, now and forever.
strings.BOL_Fiances_Of_Death_desc:
While the Mining Wars may be over, the violence in Bolivia continues. Horrified at the revolutionary reforms of the National Revolution, a collection of disaffected landowners, soldiers, and other reactionaries have begun an insurgency that has rendered much of the countryside from government control. The most notorious among them is a group of terrorists nicknamed the 'Fiancés of Death'. Radicalized by contacts with the international fascist organizations and funded by a reinvigorated drug trade they have struck terror into the countryside, targeting alleged supporters of the new regime.

With economic and political woes abound, the revolutionary government has been able to do little to counter this threat, leading many to question its long-term viability.
strings.BOL_The_True_National_Revolution_desc:
While the MNR has long promised a national revolution for Bolivia, it was Juan José Torres who was able to finally achieve it. Large chunks of the country's vast mining wealth have been nationalized and a People's Assembly has been formed to carry out sweeping left-wing political and social reforms. The Bolivian nation will finally be restored to its rightful owners: the people.

And yet all is not well. These sweeping changes have also necessitated the purging of large sections of the government and military hindering their efficacy and driving dissent and emigration. But worst of all, Bolivia's neighbors conspire to crush the revolution in its cradle, creating an economic blockade that has crippled the nation's economy. The dreams of the Bolivian people hang in the balance.
strings.BOL_A_National_Reaction_desc:
With the coming of a new much more moderate regime to La Paz many fear or hope for the undoing of Torres's regime's vast program of reforms. However, both sides have been left disappointed. In an effort to balance his shaky political position President Guevara has undone and retained elements of the National Revolution in equal measure.

Nonetheless, with each passing day, the strength of the left wing dissipates harried by paramilitary violence from the Fiancés of Death and increasing frosty relations with the regime. For how long this balancing act will be maintained is still an open question.
strings.BOL_Bolivia_Open_For_Business_desc:
The combination of the harsh protectionist policies of the Torres regime and its international isolation nearly shattered the export-oriented economy of Bolivia. But now with the new moderate nationalist government of Guevara, things are slowly returning to normal. Though the government still has a heavy hand over the economy, the lucrative mining industry is once again open to exploitation.

But rare metals aren't the only product coming and going from Bolivia these days. The legacy of the anti-Torres insurgency has entrenched Bolivia in the international drug trade, as its still untamed hinterland has become a trade hub for Manchurian opioids and the emerging cash crop of Cocaine.
strings.BOL_Dual_Yoke_desc:
Can allies of convenience really be allies at all? The question rings out to the diplomatic core of Brazil and Chile following their joint ejection from the business of Bolivia's exploitation, cut out of their slice of the pie by greed disguised as virtue, celebrated by men of industry as those under them sweated profit in lamplit mines. But greed does not stop at an exact percentage; it boils, waiting for the next slice that can be stolen.

As weeks turn to months, hungry eyes from both Brazil and Chile seem certain to look with longing at the other's Bolivian holdings, salivating at the chance of a more efficient imperialism. The hopeful among them pray that it can be averted. The bold believe it belongs solely to one nation. The Bolivians can only continue to despair.
strings.BOL_La_Ruta_Del_Plata_desc: When the Spaniards lorded over the Americas, the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata functioned as an epicenter for plunderers and scoundrels alike - taking their booty across the Andes downstream for distribution and supplying. Nowadays, the Argentinians appear keen to revive this colonial legacy in deplorable self-interest, as Buenos Aires receives much of their ill-gotten riches from the tumultuous Bolivian nation with little regard for retribution.
strings.BOL_Jaguars_Prey_desc:
Instead of chasing after their prey like the Cheetahs and Lions of Africa, the Jaguars that roam South America stalk their prey, waiting for opportunities to ambush. Then, a powerful bite to the back of the head brings the animal down. Then, their fangs tear away flesh and slurp up the still-warm blood.

Much like a Jaguar, Brazil has stalked Bolivia, waiting for economic vulnerability to pounce. Its fangs tear away our precious metals, and they guzzle our natural gas. It's an animal world, and Bolivia finds itself at the bottom of the food chain.
strings.BOL_In_The_Condors_Nest_desc:
The Andean Condor is a scavenger, not a bird of prey. Their feet and legs are relatively weak, making them unable to hunt or fight eagles over hunting grounds. Instead, they seek out carcasses of large animals or wounded smaller animals to feed their spawn.

Like a condor, Chile has kidnapped Bolivia from the ground and taken us to their nest to feed their young. The mining and natural gas companies of Chile squawk and clamor for their chance to feed on the prey their father brought.
strings.BOL_Military_Peasant_Alliance_desc: Whatever damages the army have done in the past, now is the time to rectify those mistakes. The outsiders who bring false accusations concerning the mistreatment of the peasantry will be satisfied knowing a pact has finally materialized. From now on, the government promises to cease all hostilities and fund private plantations with socioeconomic aid. In exchange, all that is required is for those farmers to cooperate in ending the division that has undone Bolivia for the past three decades.
strings.BOL_Paz_Orden_Y_Progreso_desc: A product of spiritual poverty is an intense unwillingness to pursue society's greater good. Unfortunately, the Bolivian peasantry became infected by this sort of pestilence. There is no 'cure' as reformists suggest, and giving a spineless compromise will not return productivity to those lazy beggars. For Bolivia to become peaceful again, their slander against the government deserves repression, and they will return to their proper place of toiling in the fields with no more carrots and sticks.
strings.BOL_Fury_Of_The_Old_Guard_desc: The disorganization of FSB's ranks has brought out the worst scenario envisioned. With the sacred ideal of Falange now usurped by the unsightly Rioja, there is nothing more to halt the degeneration of the Bolivian civilization. But despair is an ideology of the frail, and Únzaga's type knows better than to cede power freely to someone so feckless and unreasonable. It will only be through the most brutal of political struggles that the true sons of Bolivia regain the god-given right to rule.
strings.BOL_The_Undying_Flame_desc: Rioja thought he could choose to betray the revolution, but there was no good ending for the backstabber. For the civilized peoples, most found his deviation abhorrent and Napoleonism palpable. However, such treachery only allowed a baptism of fire to the loyal White Shirts, with Óscar Únzaga bearing the torch of Falange to witness a rebirth of the Bolivian nation. Now that the Great Work reigns triumphant, all shall witness a Bolivia without Chilean savagery built upon morality and might.
strings.BOL_The_Declawed_Eagle_desc: For an unaware Chilean observer, with the FSB's continuous presence, Bolivia's future appears as grim as ever. Yet something has changed. The institution grew more open and democratic, and years of militarism have finally become a topic of the past. Diplomatic operators in Santiago sigh in relief following their resounding success in taming the Falangist mechanism. But even the most naive optimists still question whether it's just a masquerade, biding time to rear its ugly head again.

strings.BOL_mining_war_category_desc_BRA: The situation in Bolivia has grown dire. Our ally General Candía's government is under threat by a mélange of foes: armed mining syndicates, Falangist exiles, and Nationalist remnants.“
strings.BOL_mining_war_help_text_BRA:
While General Candía's coup has been an unexpected turn in our favor in Bolivia, the so-called “mining wars” in response are threatening to undo our gains.

A variety of forces, from Falangist exiles to Nationalist remnants, are threatening to overthrow the government and install a new one. As the time to launch their plan draws near, we must act to secure the loyalty of a majority of the nation's five key groups.

The triangular diagram below plots the loyalties of each of the key groups: Police, Laborers, Military, Peasants, and Elites. Groups in the green Government region have our loyalty, and groups nearest to the region can be most easily convinced.

strings.BOL_mining_war_falangists_tooltip:
Falangists

The FSB represents the alternative to those patriots in Bolivia who hate the Oligarchs and the MNR. People might mock them for their fascist ideas, but the Falangists stand proud as the second force in Bolivia.

The Falangists control [?BOL.BOL_CHL_groups_won] key groups
strings.BOL_mining_war_nationalists_tooltip:
Nationalists

The Nationalists are the main opposition group in Bolivia to the Oligarchs, they are rallied behind the MNR, a big-tent party that ranges from the conservative right to the Marxist left.

The Nationalists control [?BOL.BOL_ARG_groups_won] key groups
strings.BOL_mining_war_government_tooltip:
Government

And above all: every policeman knows that though governments may change, the police remains. To their detractors, the Government represents the same oligarchy that has brought ruin to Bolivia.

The Government control [?BOL.BOL_BRA_groups_won] key groups
strings.BOL_mining_war_winner_tooltip: Any faction that controls at least three of the five key groups will prevail once the crisis comes to a head.
